gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 accepts only 12–60 V of solar input, so two of BLUETTI's 350 W panels (33 V Voc each, 66 V in series) can't be wired in series. Two SP200L 200 W panels (24.6 V Voc each, 49.2 V in series) fit that window.
standout_why: Neither saved chat listed any search results, so there was no rival page to compare against. That leaves ChatGPT's own answer. It recommends '4 × 500W panels' with a 'compatible MPPT charge controller' but never gives a controller's input voltage window or how many panels can go in series. The 60 V ceiling decides which BLUETTI bundle to buy and how to wire it: the $1,499 2×200 W bundle wires in series, while the $2,148 2×350 W bundle has to be wired in parallel. This set covers ChatGPT's 'small weekend cabin' size from its first chat (400–800 W of panels, 2–5 kWh, 1–2 kW inverter), not its 48 V 3 kW example.
kit_items: Power station (battery + inverter + MPPT): BLUETTI Elite 200 V2. 2,073.6 Wh, 2,600 W AC, solar input of 12–60 V / 20 A / 1,000 W max. It fits a weekend cabin.

Solar panels: 2× BLUETTI SP200L 200 W wired in series. 2 × 24.6 V Voc = 49.2 V, which is under the 60 V input ceiling with 10.8 V of headroom. Wired in parallel they would reach 2 × 10.8 A = 21.6 A Isc, over the 20 A input limit, so series is the wiring that stays inside both limits.
Avoid for series wiring: BLUETTI 350W Solar Panel ×2 (the Elite 200 V2 + 2×350W bundle). 2 × 33 V Voc = 66 V, which exceeds the 60 V ceiling, so these must be wired in parallel.

findings.label: Open-circuit voltage
findings.note: Two in series: 2 × 33 = 66 V Voc, 6 V over the Elite 200 V2's 60 V maximum. This is the panel in BLUETTI's own Elite 200 V2+2*350W bundle. The page lists no Vmp, Isc or Imp, so the parallel-wired output can't be computed.
